editorial.headline: A Nationally Open Arts-Venue Activity, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Operating cultural centres, auditoriums and live-music venues is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks PMA registration.
editorial.body:
In Bali, a foreign investor cannot register this activity through PMA today, even though nationally it is open to 100% foreign ownership. The activity concerns the operation of places in which art is made, shown and heard: concert and theatre auditoriums, cultural centres and cultural parks, facilities that support the creation of visual art, and other arts facilities. It also covers the operation of live-music venues, music clubs and comparable facilities where artists perform. The focus is operational—the running of the venue or facility that accommodates artistic creation or live performance.

The national registration picture is broad in scale. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar businesses, covering the full range of enterprise categories stated in the record. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. For an investor considering the operating side of a cultural centre, auditorium or live-performance location, those are clear national settings. Yet the national ownership ceiling answers only the position at national level; it does not determine whether a PMA registration can be made in a particular region.

In Bali, the position is direct. The Bali designation is Blocked (risk class), and the record expressly identifies the activity as blocked. Its stated basis is the OSS risk profile at the Besar scale, where every scope is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah. Bali’s stated rule is island-wide and permanent: it blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. The recorded moratorium was issued on the thirteenth of May, twenty twenty-six, under the Governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP.

That distinction is the essential planning fact. A 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling means full foreign ownership is available nationally for this activity, but it is not a Bali-side entitlement. Here, the Bali result is a registration block under a risk-based moratorium. The practical reading is therefore clear: this is a nationally open activity that may operate across the listed scales, while a PMA route in Bali is closed.
editorial.pullQuote: A 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling is not a Bali-side entitlement when PMA registration is blocked.
